dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a measurable space Ω, a probability measure μ, a real-valued μ-integrable function X, and its integrability proof hX, this definition returns the LocalDef004 object constructed by LocalDef005 μ X hX.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the structured object whose first and second real projections occur in the two asserted equalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an object self of LocalDef004 μ X hX, this abbreviation returns its first real component, self.1, identified by the structure API as its mean.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns LocalDef001 μ X hX into the left-hand side of the first equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an object self of LocalDef004 μ X hX, this abbreviation returns its second real component, self.2, identified by the structure API as its variance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns LocalDef001 μ X hX into the left-hand side of the second equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is a type of structured objects indexed by a measurable space Ω, a probability measure μ, a real function X, and a proof that X is μ-integrable. Its constructor data consist of real mean and variance components plus proofs identifying them with the prescribed integral formulas and a centered-mean identity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of LocalDef001 and supplies the two real projections compared with the stated integrals.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given μ, X, and hX, this definition constructs a LocalDef004 object whose mean is LocalDef007 μ X, whose variance is LocalDef011 μ X, whose identification fields are the corresponding reflexive equalities, and whose centered-mean field is the identity proved by LocalDef010.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Because LocalDef001 returns this object, its first and second components are exactly the integral mean and centered second-moment formulas asserted by the target.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor accepts real numbers mean and variance, proofs that mean equals LocalDef007 μ X and variance equals LocalDef011 μ X, and a proof that the integral-defined mean of ω ↦ X ω − mean is zero; it returns a LocalDef004 object.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It specifies the structure and proof obligations used by LocalDef005, thereby fixing the semantic roles of the two projections as mean and variance.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and real-valued function X, LocalDef007 μ X is the Bochner integral ∫ X dμ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the mean stored in LocalDef001 and also the centering constant appearing inside the variance integrand.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every μ and X, this theorem is the reflexive equality LocalDef007 μ X = LocalDef007 μ X.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the proof field identifying the constructed object's mean with its prescribed integral formula; it adds no substantive assumption or result.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every μ and X, this theorem is the reflexive equality LocalDef011 μ X = LocalDef011 μ X.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the proof field identifying the constructed object's variance with its prescribed centered-square integral; it adds no substantive assumption or result.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: If μ is a probability measure and X is μ-integrable, then the integral of ω ↦ X ω − LocalDef007 μ X is zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It proves the centered-mean field required when LocalDef005 constructs LocalDef001. Its use explains the probability-measure and integrability hypotheses, although the target's two displayed equalities do not themselves mention this field.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For μ and X, LocalDef011 μ X is LocalDef007 μ applied to ω ↦ (X ω − LocalDef007 μ X)^2; equivalently, it is ∫(X−∫X dμ)^2 dμ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the variance stored as the second component of LocalDef001 and unfolds to the right-hand side of the second asserted equality.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: And P Q is the proposition that both propositions P and Q hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires the mean equality and the variance equality simultaneously.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Eq a b is equality between two objects a and b of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses both claimed identities as equalities of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the heterogeneous exponentiation operation; with the instantiated real base, natural exponent, and real result, it is ordinary natural-number exponentiation of reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With exponent 2, it squares each centered value X(ω) − ∫X dμ in the variance integrand.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the heterogeneous subtraction operation; with all involved types equal to Real, it is ordinary real subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the centered deviation X(ω) − ∫X dμ.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable

dependency_coverage.name: Nat

binders: Ω is an arbitrary type, at an arbitrary universe level.
Ω is equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω.
μ is assumed to be a probability measure.
X is an arbitrary function from Ω to the real numbers.
hX is a proof that X is integrable with respect to μ.
_hVariance is a proof that the function ω ↦ (X(ω) − ∫ X dμ)^2 is integrable with respect to μ.
hypotheses: The measure μ has total mass one, via the IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
The real-valued function X is μ-integrable: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and has finite integral of its norm.
The centered-square function ω ↦ (X(ω) − ∫ X dμ)^2 is μ-integrable.
conclusions: The mean component of LocalDef001 μ X hX equals the Bochner integral ∫ X dμ.
The variance component of LocalDef001 μ X hX equals the Bochner integral ∫ (X(ω) − ∫ X dμ)^2 dμ.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X hX is the LocalDef004 object constructed with first component m, second component v, proofs identifying those components with m and v, and a proof that ∫Ω (X(ω) − m) dμ(ω) = 0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, and every integrable real-valued function X whose squared deviation from its integral mean is also integrable, the structured object LocalDef001 μ X hX has mean exactly ∫Ω X dμ and variance exactly ∫Ω (X − ∫Ω X dμ)^2 dμ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement applies only when μ is a probability measure; it does not cover arbitrary finite, sigma-finite, or infinite measures without that instance.
X must be μ-integrable, so nonintegrable real functions are outside the quantified cases carrying hX.
The centered-square function must also be μ-integrable, which is the finite-second-moment condition relative to the integral mean; integrability of X alone does not guarantee it.
If no proof of centered-square integrability exists for a particular X, the implication has no applicable hypothesis instance for that X and is vacuously true in its implication form.

The supplied centered-square integrability proof is not used to define or prove either displayed equality: the variance formula is already stored definitionally in LocalDef001. Thus the equalities themselves remain tautological identifications even though the target assumes finite variance.
The proposition does not assert that an arbitrary independently supplied mean or variance has these values; it concerns only the specifically constructed LocalDef001 object.
The proposition does not assert nonnegativity, strict positivity, uniqueness, or any distributional property of the variance.
Because μ is a probability measure and X is integrable, the centering identity ∫(X−∫X)dμ=0 used in the structure construction is meaningful and valid.
ambiguities: The declaration gives the semantic roles of the LocalDef004 projections through its constructor and LocalDef005 fields, but the bare inductive type line alone does not independently display field names; calling the first and second projections mean and variance relies on the supplied complete constructor/body inventory.

The notation called variance here is specifically the centered second moment with denominator corresponding to the full probability measure; it is not an unbiased sample variance or a conditional variance.

The mathematical assertion is extensionally the standard mean and variance formulas, but formally both conclusions follow from how LocalDef001 was constructed rather than from the centered-square integrability hypothesis.
